paper_title: RPDR: A Round-trip Prediction-Based Data Augmentation Framework for Long-Tail Question Answering
summary:
RPDR: A Round-trip Prediction-Based Data Augmentation Framework for Long-Tail Question Answering - Yiming Zhang, Siyue Zhang, Junbo Zhao, Chen Zhao, 2025

RPDR targets the failure mode of dense retrievers on long-tail open-domain QA, where rare entities are poorly represented and BM25 often outperforms embedding-based retrieval on infrequent queries. The objective is to make dense retrieval competitive or superior in long-tail settings by augmenting training with synthetic question answer pairs that are not merely relevant, but easy for the retriever to internalize. The framework has three stages. First, it synthesizes long-tail QA pairs from Wikidata triples aligned to Wikipedia, filtering for low-popularity subjects using monthly page views below 1e6 and retaining only cases where BM25 top-1000 passages contain the answer string; this yields about 86k augmentation samples for PopQA and 126k for EntityQuestions. Second, it trains an inverse embedding model following the vec2text formulation of Morris et al. to reconstruct text from a dense retriever embedding. For each synthetic question x, an off-the-shelf dense retriever produces e(x), the inverse model decodes a reconstruction x hat, and a round-trip score S(x) = 1 minus the normalized L2 distance between phi(x hat) and phi(x) is used to select samples whose embeddings are recoverable, operationalizing “easy-to-learn” data. Third, a new dense retriever is trained on this filtered augmentation set, initialized from Contriever. The method is evaluated on PopQA and EntityQuestions, both grounded in Wikidata and partitioned by entity frequency. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17366?utm_source=openai))

The retrieval gains are large on the exact regime where prior work found dense retrieval weakest. On PopQA long-tail queries, RPDR reaches R@10 74.5 and R@20 75.7, versus BM25 at 62.6 and 66.8, Contriever at 52.3 and 59.3, and NV-Embed at 55.0 and 62.3; the paper reports this as a 19.5 point R@10 gain over NV-Embed and an 11.9 point gain over BM25. On EntityQuestions long-tail queries, RPDR attains R@10 54.6 versus BM25 48.3 and Contriever 42.9. The round-trip selector is materially responsible for the improvement: on PopQA long-tail, RPDR exceeds an otherwise matched random-sampling variant by 7.7 R@10 points, 74.5 versus 66.8. These retrieval gains transfer to end-to-end RAG accuracy across multiple readers. With GPT-3.5 as generator on PopQA long-tail, exact match rises to 41.4 for RPDR, compared with 30.5 for BM25, 29.7 for Contriever, and 22.7 for parametric-only generation; the paper highlights an 11.7 point gain over Contriever in this setting. Qualitative analysis shows the method is strongest on syntactically simple but semantically rare entities and weaker on syntactically complex names, motivating a learned router that switches between RPDR and BM25. That routing module is implemented as a Sentence-BERT binary classifier trained on 10,000 augmented examples for 5 epochs with AdamW and 2e-5 learning rate, and further lifts PopQA long-tail retrieval from R@10 74.5 to 79.1 and EntityQuestions long-tail from 54.6 to 58.4. ([aclanthology.org](https://aclanthology.org/2025.emnlp-main.1119.pdf))
